policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'your evil doings' does not distinguish the qere וּמַעֲלְלֵיכֶם from the ketiv ומעליליכם; no mapped textual note is supplied, so both readings remain compatible and the base qere carries the projection.

ASV's 'a line shall be stretched forth over Jerusalem' does not distinguish the qere וְקָו from the ketiv וקוה; no mapped textual note is supplied, so both readings remain compatible and the base qere carries the projection.
